newsitem.title: USA: Secure Computing okays holder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Secure Computing okays holder rights plan.

text.p: Secure Computing Corp said Friday its board of directors approved a shareholder rights plan.

Jeff Waxman, chairman and chief executive of Secure Computing, said there is no reason to believe anyone is currently considering a takeover of the company, calling the plan a "prudent step" for a growing company.
"The shareholder rights plan is intended to increase the likelihood that the company's stockholders will realize the long-term value of their investment in Secure," Waxman said.

Under the plan, the company will distribute as a dividend one right for each of the company's outstanding shares on August 15. It will also distribute one right of Secure Computing Canada Ltd, which is exchangeable for the company's common stock.

The rights are exercisable only if a person or group were to acquire 15 percent or more the Secure's oustanding stock, including exchangeable shares, or announce a tender or exchange offer that would result in a 15 percent or more stake.
Secure Computing is a network security company.
